text:
maya: Heads-up — we just got a Customer Success escalation: several customers on Growth tier are seeing intermittent 429s since the limit push an hour ago. They report token failures in production. @liam can you confirm?
liam: seeing spike in 429s in the rate-limiter logs, mostly for requests with header `X-Customer-Tier: growth` and `X-Customer-Id` cluster 37xx. Not all growth tenants, looks shard-affine. :frowning:
jason: logs show `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` with window=60s and burst=20; the rollout reduced burst from 40 -> 20 as part of the staged policy. I pushed the change at ~1945675000 via rollout-bot.
emma: customer-facing thread: they noticed errors at 14:12 UTC and escalated at 14:18. One of them provided a repro with 200ms median but then 429s at high qps.
maya: can we get a quick mitigation? we need to stop impacting paying customers while we decide whether to rollback.
liam: options: full rollback of the ratepolicy PR (easy), or targeted whitelist increase for the affected customer shard (requires a small override config). I'd prefer targeted if it's fast.
jason: agree. I can apply a transient override: set `burst=40` for header `X-Customer-Shard: shard-37` for 30m. That should admit current inflight without opening the floodgates.
liam: please go ahead. Patch looks like:```
{
  "matcher": { "header": "X-Customer-Shard", "value": "shard-37" },
  "overrides": { "burst": 40, "window_sec": 60 }
}
```
rollout-bot: deploy triggered: revert candidate not needed — applying config override to rate-limiter-service on cluster "us-east-1".
jason: applied override to shard-37, logs now show 200 -> 429 ratio improving. I can watch metrics for the next 10 minutes.
maya: confirmed with CS: one of the Growth customers reports success after ~3 minutes, other still intermittent but much better. Good call.
harpreet: filing incident note: this was caused by the staged policy that reduced burst for all Growth tenants. It looks like certain high-variance customers need an exception. I'll add to the postmortem.
liam: long term we should gate these policy changes behind traffic-profile testing: replay or synthetic traffic per shard. Also add a canary segment by `X-Customer-Shard` rather than global tier knob.
emma: can we also prepare a brief customer message? We should acknowledge and say we rolled a temporary override and are working on a permanent fix.
maya: yes i'll coordinate comms with CS.
sre-bot: alert suppressed: 429 spike for rule "ratepolicy-v3" on shard-37 — override applied.
jason: two follow-ups: 1) I'll revert override after a controlled test run tomorrow morning if we have the adjusted profile; 2) we'll open PR to change rollout strategy: add header-aware canaries and a safety multiplier that keeps burst=baseline for top N shards during rollout.
liam: can you also add a quick metric query into the runbook to track `sum(429s) by shard` and a Grafana panel alert that triggers if > 1% of requests for a tenant hit 429 in a 5m window?
jason: will do. Pushing PR link in a bit.
maya: thanks team. For the incident timeline: 14:12 initial customer error -> 14:18 escalation -> 14:25 detection by eng -> 14:32 override applied -> 14:35 customer confirms improvement. We'll run postmortem tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
liam: note for postmortem: consider adding staged rollback path to rollout-bot so we can flip back policy per-shard quickly. Current rollback is repo-level which is coarse.
emma: assigning CS follow-up to @maya to send customer note after postmortem draft is ready.
maya: on it.
rollout-bot: deployment log: config-override applied (id:cfg-7742), expires in 30m unless extended.
jason: metrics look stable. closing this thread but keeping postmortem todo open. :thumbsup:
